numberItems.stem: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, how much pressure should the compressor build?
options: At least 55 psi in either system
At least 85 psi in both systems
At least 100 psi in both systems
numberItems.explanation: Let the compressor build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems; the warning shutting off (above 55 psi) is not enough (p. 5-6).

numberItems.stem: In a dual air system, the low-air warning should come on before pressure falls below what level in either system?
numberItems.explanation: The warning should come on before either system drops below 55 psi; 45 psi is the top of the spring brake range (pp. 5-6, 5-9).

numberItems.stem: You pull hard on an S-cam slack adjuster. How far can it move where the push rod attaches before it likely needs adjusting?
numberItems.explanation: If it moves more than about 1 inch where the push rod attaches, it probably needs adjustment; ¼ inch is the lining minimum and ½ is the drum crack limit (p. 5-7).

numberItems.stem: Automatic slack adjusters are on all vehicles built since which year?
numberItems.explanation: All vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjusters, and you must still check them (p. 5-7).

numberItems.stem: A brake drum (or disc) is not safe if it has a crack longer than what?
options: ½ the width of the friction area
1/4 the width of the friction area
numberItems.explanation: Drums and discs must not have cracks longer than ½ the width of the friction area (p. 5-7).

numberItems.stem: Brake linings must not be worn thinner than what?
numberItems.explanation: Linings must not be worn thinner than ¼ inch, loose, or soaked with oil or grease (p. 5-7).

numberItems.stem: For the applied leakage test, you first build air pressure to governor cut-out. What range does the handbook give for cut-out here?
numberItems.explanation: The applied leakage test starts at governor cut-out, 120–140 psi or the maker's level (p. 5-8).

numberItems.stem: In the applied leakage test, how long do you hold the foot brake fully down?
numberItems.explanation: Hold the brake for 1 minute after the gauge settles, watching the gauge and listening for leaks; 45 seconds and 3 minutes are buildup-test limits (pp. 5-8–5-9).

numberItems.stem: Applied leakage test: what is the most pressure a combination of 3 or more vehicles may lose in 1 minute?
numberItems.explanation: Applied limits: 3 psi single, 4 psi for 2 vehicles, 6 psi for 3 or more; 5 psi is the static limit for 3 or more (pp. 5-8, 5-10).

numberItems.stem: Applied leakage test: a tractor tows a trailer with electric brakes (no air brakes). What is the most it may lose in 1 minute?
numberItems.explanation: When the towed vehicles have no air brakes, the applied limit is 3 psi; 2 psi is the static limit for that case (pp. 5-8, 5-10).

numberItems.stem: In the spring brake test, at about what pressure should the parking brake valve (and tractor protection valve) pop out?
numberItems.explanation: The valves should pop out at normally 20–45 psi; 55–75 psi is the low-air warning range and 80–85 psi the common bus warning (pp. 5-8–5-9).

numberItems.stem: On a triple reservoir bus, you do the drive-forward spring brake check if the parking brake valve hasn't popped out by about what pressure?
numberItems.explanation: If the valve hasn't popped out by about 20 psi, show that the spring brakes came on by trying to drive forward (single vehicles only) (p. 5-9).

numberItems.stem: At normal idle, how fast should air pressure build in a dual air system?
options: From about 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes
From about 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds
From about 85 to 100 psi within 3 minutes
numberItems.explanation: Dual systems should build from about 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds; 50 to 90 psi in 3 minutes is for pre-1975 single systems (p. 5-9).

numberItems.stem: On a single air system (pre-1975 vehicle), how fast should air pressure build at normal idle?
options: From about 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes
From about 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds
From about 50 to 90 psi within 45 seconds
numberItems.explanation: Pre-1975 single systems should build from about 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes; 85 to 100 psi in 45 seconds is for dual systems (p. 5-9).

numberItems.stem: Static leakage test (engine off, brakes released): what is the most a combination of 2 vehicles may lose in 1 minute?
numberItems.explanation: Static limits: 2 psi single, 3 psi for 2 vehicles, 5 psi for 3 or more; 4 psi is the applied limit for 2 vehicles (pp. 5-8, 5-10).

numberItems.stem: Static leakage test: a truck tows a trailer that has no air brakes. What is the most it may lose in 1 minute?
numberItems.explanation: With towed units that have no air brakes, the static limit is 2 psi; 3 psi is the applied limit for that case (pp. 5-8, 5-10).
